steps: Close both of your hands into loose fists in front of your body.
Shake the fists in small, quick movements from side to side.
Keep the trembling motion tight and close to your torso.
Hunch your shoulders up toward your ears while the hands shake.
Pull your chin in with a bracing expression, as if winter air is hitting you.
tip: The same sign doubles for 'freezing' — a shivering body is the whole picture.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your chest.
Angle the hands so the fingertips meet above the middle.
Touch the fingertips together to form the shape of a roof.
Keep the fingertips joined briefly, then gently release the shape.
Hold your arms steady with a calm, settled expression throughout.
tip: BSL uses the HOUSE sign for 'home' too — one roof-shaped sign covers both words.

steps: Open both hands in front of your body at chest height.
Touch the tip of each index finger to the tip of its thumb.
Hold both rounded shapes up, palms facing down and out.
Move the hands side to side in small, smooth arcs.
Keep the arcs gentle and rhythmic, as if conducting an orchestra.
tip: Picture a conductor's hands — the flicking arcs are the rhythm of the music.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand up with only the little finger extended.
Open your dominant hand flat in front of your body.
Move the open dominant hand forwards until it touches the little finger.
Make one clean contact, then stop the movement crisply and completely.
Keep a neutral, settled expression as the dominant hand lands.
tip: The little finger is the end of the line — touching it marks the last one.

steps: Hold your dominant hand in front of your body, palm sideways.
Extend only your thumb upward, with the fingers loosely closed.
Twist the hand once at the wrist in a small, neat flick.
Keep the motion short — one twist, not a repeated shake.
Mouth the word 'next' clearly as the thumb flicks over.
tip: The same sign is taught for 'neighbour' — the flicked thumb points to whoever is next to you.

steps: Extend the index and middle fingers of your dominant hand together.
Press the tips of the two fingers lightly against your forehead.
Twist the hand forwards at the wrist in one smooth turn.
Finish with the fingertips pointing forwards, in front of your face.
Keep the elbow relaxed and mouth the word 'name' as you twist.
tip: The two-finger 'N' touches the forehead — names live in the head, then come forward.

steps: Close your dominant hand into a fist with the index finger extended.
Turn the pointing finger back toward your own chest centre.
Aim the fingertip at the centre of your chest, holding it briefly.
Keep the palm turned sideways; the direction of the point is what matters.
Stay still and look at the viewer as you hold the point.
tip: One sign does 'me' and 'I' — pointing at yourself always means the speaker.

steps: Hold your dominant hand up in front of your body at chest height.
Extend the index and middle fingers straight up together in a V.
Hold the hand steady so the two fingers are clearly separate.
Let the fingers point straight upward without twisting the wrist.
Mouth the word 'two' as you hold the handshape steady.
tip: BSL numbers 1 to 5 are one-handed — two upright fingers is all 'two' needs.
